note.after_visit_summary: You came in because you've been feeling fluttering or skipped beats in your chest for about three weeks, mostly at night. We talked about your habits and found you're drinking a lot of caffeine—about four cold brews and two energy drinks each day—and getting only about five hours of sleep. Your exam and ECG were normal. The fluttering is likely from extra heart beats, which are common and usually harmless, but can be triggered by too much caffeine, energy drinks, and not enough sleep. To help, cut back caffeine slowly over two weeks to avoid headaches: have no more than one regular coffee a day and stop energy drinks completely. Try to sleep at least seven hours each night. We're checking your thyroid, blood count, and electrolytes with lab tests. If the fluttering doesn't improve in six weeks after these changes, we may have you wear a heart monitor for two weeks. Go to the emergency room if you faint, have chest pain with the fluttering, or feel a racing heartbeat that won't stop. Otherwise, return to the clinic in six weeks for follow-up.
